stem: Tatenda runs a car-repair workshop in Mutare as a sole trader. Profit last year was US\$14,400. His friend Sipho, a trained auto-electrician, offers to join him as a partner and invest US\$6,000 for new diagnostic equipment. Sipho suggests sharing profits equally.

parts.label: (a)

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which would remain the same for Tatenda if he formed the partnership?

options.content: He would still keep all the profit
options.rationale: Profit would be shared.

options.rationale: Partners share decisions.

options.content: He would still have unlimited liability
options.rationale: Correct: general partners have unlimited liability.

options.rationale: Sipho adds capital.

parts.label: (d)

For: shared workload and responsibility (1)

Justified conclusion (1)

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Sipho's capital and skills would let the workshop repair modern cars, which could bring in many new customers. But on equal shares profit would need to double just for Tatenda to earn what he earns now, and equal shares ignore the customers he has already built up. Tatenda should accept a partnership only with a written deed that gives him a larger share or a salary first.

stem: Rudo makes and sells jewellery from home in Bulawayo. She needs little capital, wants full control of her designs and has few debts. Her cousin Thandeka, who runs an online shop, suggests they form a partnership.

parts.label: (a)

Unlimited liability / keeps all the profit / no separate legal identity (1)

points.description: Advantage 1, e.g. Thandeka's online shop gives access to more customers (1)
Developed: higher sales and profit (1)
Advantage 2, e.g. shared workload / more capital / new skills (1)
Developed: Rudo can focus on design (1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend whether Rudo should remain a sole trader or form a partnership. Justify your answer.

points.description: Sole trader: keeps full control of designs, which she values (1)
Sole trader: keeps all the profit; little capital needed, so no need for a partner (1)
Partnership: online reach could raise sales a lot (1)
Partnership: must share profit and decisions; risk of disputes; unlimited liability for partner's debts (1)
Alternative, e.g. sell through Thandeka's shop on commission without a partnership (1)
Justified recommendation (1)

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Rudo values control of her designs and needs little capital, so the main reasons for a partnership (capital and shared decisions) do not apply. A partnership would also make her liable for any debts of Thandeka's shop. However, Thandeka's online customers could increase her sales. Rudo should remain a sole trader and sell through Thandeka's online shop on a commission basis, gaining the customers without giving up control.

explanation: A recommendation must use the case: Rudo's need for control, low capital needs and the online sales opportunity.
hints: Is there a way to gain the customers without a partnership?
